questions: Must State 5 remain free to choose how bound inputs are represented, or must it preserve M20's already stated requirement that they are kept by digest?

Must Registry compare the actual bound values, or may equality of the digest required by M20 and A16 stand for equality even when distinct inputs have the same digest? The texts must reconcile this absolute refusal guarantee with M20's “the inputs it is bound to, by their digest” and A16's digest binding.
May State 5 choose the representation of confirmation bindings, or must it retain the digest representation already required by M20 and by A16 for the import?

quotes:
A session holds at most one pending confirmation (A13 rule 6); a
submission whose action, target, version or inputs differ from those shown
is not bound (A13 rule 6, test 12) — the inputs are kept as their digest,
this operation's way of binding them, never as values; the value never
appears in a URL, a log line, a diagnostic or an entry (A13 rule 7).
judgement.why: State 5 expressly chooses digest-only retention and supplies the submitted inputs as a digest to the confirmation comparison, so generation does not choose the representation.
options: Keep confirmation inputs only as their fixed-order digest.
Keep the structured values or a collision-resolving representation.
consequences: The later design selects digest equality as the confirmation operation's comparison representation while retaining the stated refusal guarantee.

topics.topic: A04 stage and refusal precedence for confirmation expiry or binding mismatch
questions: At which A04 stage are an expired confirmation and a mismatch of its bound action, target, version or inputs checked, and which refusal is returned when one coincides with a later failure such as a nonexistent target, invalid input or stale revision?

At which A04 rule 6 stage is a mismatch between the submitted action, target, version or inputs and the pending confirmation answered: stage (1) as part of the confirmation check, or at the native stage of the mismatching target, value or version?

quotes: | `confirmation_refused` | (1) | `confirmation_not_pending` — the session holds no pending value: never shown, used up or cleared; `confirmation_other_value` — another value while the pending one is valid, which stays; `confirmation_bound_elsewhere` — the pending value given for another action, target, revision or inputs, now used up; `confirmation_expired` — cleared (A13 rule 6) | the owner submits the pending step again, or has it shown again |
judgement.why: State 5 assigns expiry and every action, target, revision or input binding mismatch to stage (1), ahead of existence, value and stale-revision failures.
options: Answer expiry and every binding mismatch at stage (1).
Answer a mismatch at the native stage of the target, value or revision.
consequences: The owner receives `confirmation_refused` before any later-stage failure, and a supplied pending value is consumed as A13 specifies.

topics.topic: Complete set of import values bound by confirmation
questions: Are the import confirmation's bound inputs only the file digest and picks, or do they also include every submitted name, alias and Customer value as A16 requires?

Is the import confirmation bound only to the file digest and ordered picks named here, or also to every name, alias, Customer name, kind, tax-id choice and other Customer value that A16 rules 2 and 6 say the mapping showed and bound? The complete import input set must be stated.

quotes:
The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
   step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.

The file and the
   picks are bound by their digest, the names, aliases and Customer values
   with them, so the mapping it builds is the one the step showed but for
   the ids production gained in between;
judgement.why: A16 expressly includes the names, aliases and Customer values alongside the file and picks and says the confirmation applies nothing else.
options: Bind the file digest, picks, names, aliases and Customer values.
Bind only the file digest and picks.
consequences: Changing any displayed name, alias or Customer value makes the submitted binding differ and causes refusal.

topics.topic: Contract-visible and hidden representation for retaining and comparing confirmation bindings
questions: What representation and module obligation will State 5 use to retain and compare the action, target, version and inputs bound by a confirmation step?

State 5 must decide what bound facts callers supply to and may rely on from the owner-session operation; generation must choose the hidden representation without weakening the required comparison. Which contract-visible value and hidden representation are used?

quotes:
The admitted session; the action; its target; the revision or access
version the step shows, or that it shows none; the action's inputs — for an
erasure its choice, for the import the upload's number and the file's
digest with the picks, names, aliases and Customer values, for an erasure
of old entries the date.

The session's pending confirmation is replaced: a new value from
`random_values.make_secret_value`, bound to the action, its target, what the
step showed and the digest of its inputs in a fixed order, and the reading
of `clock.monotonic_reading` it was shown at.
judgement.why: State 5 defines the contract-visible structured binding supplied when the step is shown and the fixed-order digest retained and compared by the owner-session operation.
options: Pass structured action-specific inputs and retain their fixed-order digest.
Pass canonical bytes or retain the complete semantic snapshot.
consequences: The selected contract exposes the complete action-specific inputs at step creation but retains and later accepts their digest for comparison.

topics.topic: Whether confirmation binds a specific upload occurrence or only identical file bytes
questions: Does confirmation bind the particular uploaded-file occurrence, including its upload number, or only its bytes' digest?
What State 5 obligation lets the owner-session operation distinguish the upload shown by the confirmation step from a later upload of the same bytes, since their file digest and picks can be equal?

quotes:
Facts: its bytes, as uploaded; their digest, by which the mapping names the
file (A16 rule 2); and its upload number within the session, so that an upload
of the same bytes is still another upload and a confirmation step binds the
upload it showed (owner, 2026-11-24; `60_contracts.md`).

Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded in the session is
   refused: the file it named is no longer kept — also when the new file has
   the same bytes.
judgement.why: M21 makes the upload number part of the uploaded-file value specifically so identical bytes uploaded again are a different occurrence, and A16 requires the old confirmation to be refused.
options: Bind the upload occurrence through its upload number as well as its digest.
Bind only the file digest.
consequences: A later upload invalidates the old confirmation even when its bytes and digest are identical.

topics.topic: Formal invariant expressing confirmation-binding refusal and its required test
questions: What formal invariant states this new refusal guarantee, and which invariant must Required test 12 say it shows?

quotes:
a submission whose action, target, version or inputs
   differ from those the step showed is refused (test 12).

A pending confirmation shown for one action, target, version and inputs
    is refused, and used up, when the submission carrying its value changes
    any one of them: another action, another target, another version or
    none, another value of any input, or the same list in another order
    (rule 6).
judgement.why: The normative rule and Required test already permit no accepting outcome for a changed binding, so no two-outcome witness can be built, although the texts do not say whether to add one formal invariant or several or name such an invariant as what test 12 shows.
judgement.owner_question: Must A13 rule 6's binding-refusal guarantee be promoted to one formal invariant or several, and which invariant or invariants must Required test 12 say it shows?
options: Add one formal invariant covering every bound component and say test 12 shows it.
Add separate invariants for action, target, version and inputs and say which test-12 cases show each.
Leave the guarantee as a normative rule with a behavioral Required test but no formal invariant.
consequences: The first two choices make the invariant-to-test relationship explicit; the last preserves product behavior but leaves the requested formal-invariant organization unstated.
judgement.requirement_missing: no accepted requirement distinguishes the outcomes, or the product choice itself is missing; the author must establish the owner, not infer permitted freedom from silence

topics.topic: Number and reuse of monotonic and UTC clock readings per operation
questions: For each operation, how many monotonic and UTC wall-clock readings are taken, and which results must reuse the same reading?

quotes:
An operation that records an instant
  or compares a date takes the action's instant and today's date as inputs:
  `operations` reads the instant once with `clock.recorded_now` when the
  transaction begins and takes today as that instant's UTC date ("Time");
  the operation reads no clock.

Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then — the reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading` this operation takes when it is called, which for
an upload is after its bounded head has been read (A13 rule 2): a session that has
reached 8 hours from sign-in or 30 minutes without a request, or is marked
signed out, serves no request;

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing.
judgement.why: State 5 fixes one UTC reading for an action and its derived date, one monotonic reading for owner-request admission, and one shared monotonic reading for an expiry pass.
options: Reuse one applicable reading for every decision and write of an operation.
Take fresh readings at individual checks and writes.
Specify sampling separately by operation.
consequences: The later design selects operation-specific sampling and prevents an action's instant and UTC date, or a pass's session decisions, from straddling clock readings.

topics.topic: Representation, unit, and comparison domain of owner-session monotonic readings

quotes:
One reading in nanoseconds, comparable only with other readings of the same
process.
judgement.why: This is the unchanged question already judged in P3 about the representation, unit and comparison domain of monotonic readings.
options: Use an opaque monotonic-instant type.
Use an integer nanosecond reading from a process-local origin.
Use floating-point seconds from a process-local origin.
consequences: P3 records that State 5 selected process-local integer nanoseconds and comparisons only within the same process.
